design_rationale:
[0 Draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"task": 1, "key": "env_0020_national_network_airline/companion_certificates_and_passes/1", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [4, 4, 5, 4]}. The companion fare takes 5 factors; the taxes, the phone fee and the phone fee refund take 4. Occupied by task 0: the voluntary-cancellation settlement (fare, surcharge and taxes refunds and the reinstatement fee) with its four tools. This task claims the remaining four policies - companion_ext_booking_companion_fare, companion_ext_booking_phone_fee, companion_ext_booking_taxes_and_fees and companion_ext_crestline_cancel_phone_fee_refund - and their four tools, so the two scopes are disjoint and cover all eight policies; nothing is left idle.

[1 Why this is a good test] The caller wants to pay what is outstanding on his wife's companion ticket after a declined card, naming only the taxes and fees the email mentioned. The taxes rule states that the taxes of a booking are fixed only after its companion fare charge stands and, for a call-center booking, not until its phone booking fee charge stands; the phone fee rule states it is fixed only after the phone fee refund owed on every booking Crestline cancelled stands. The agent must find the March Crestline cancellation in the ledger, refund part of that booking's standing phone fee over the claim window, charge a phone fee that the remaining standing fee partly covers, charge the companion fare with five factors, and only then the taxes, whose call-center base includes the fare and the fee just paid - three of the four writes being the customer's own payments handed over at their place in the order.

[2 Policies, lineage, triggers] All four are state_due: a recorded booking owes its charges and a booking Crestline cancelled owes its phone fee refund, whoever calls. Charges cite companion_booking_rules, companion_cancellation and companion_designation (subject companion_fare_charge) and override, clause by clause, 'The holder pays companion_base_fare_usd', 'and phone_booking_fee_usd when booked through the call center, each as its own charge entry' and 'the companion's taxes and fees when companion_pays_taxes is true'. The refund cites companion_cancellation and companion_refund_controls and overrides 'phone booking fees are not refunded' and 'a refund equals the amount of the charge it names'. The refund_once gate is inherited and carried; no base gate applies to a charge entry.

[3 Factor cards] PHONE FEE REFUND: phone_refund_claim_window_method (method): latest reinstatement crestline_cancellation 2026-03-05, 54 days -> pro-rated 10.63; the baseline (nothing refunded) gives 0.00. | phone_refund_status_uplift (parameter, cross-difficulty loyalty): Summit Gold -> 10 percent; baseline 0 gives 12.22. | phone_refund_membership_age_uplift (parameter, cross-difficulty loyalty): enrolled 2016-09-02, 115 months -> 5 percent; baseline 0 gives 12.76. | phone_refund_lounge_uplift (parameter, cross-difficulty club): Summit Club Executive -> 10 percent; baseline 0 gives 12.22. | non-factor: standing_fee_for_refund = 14.50; result = 13.29. || PHONE FEE: phone_fee_rebooking_context_method (method): Crestline reinstatement 53 days before the booking -> x0.5 = 12.50; the baseline (25.00 as published) gives 16.79. | phone_fee_repeat_call_center (parameter): 2 call-center bookings in 12 months -> +20 percent; baseline 0 gives 4.54. | phone_fee_status_waiver (parameter, cross-difficulty loyalty): Summit Gold -> 30 percent; baseline 0 gives 10.79. | phone_fee_card_credit (parameter, cross-difficulty loyalty): 46000.00 co-brand miles in 12 months (the 2025-04-20 accrual is outside) -> 3.00; baseline 0 gives 9.29. | non-factor: raw_phone_fee = 7.50; standing_phone_fees = 1.21 (after the refund); result = 6.29. || COMPANION FARE: companion_fare_booking_ahead_method (method): booked 64 days ahead -> 119 x 0.9 = 107.10; the baseline (119.00 as published) gives 82.86. | companion_fare_activity_discount (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty loyalty): 13760.00 qualifying dollars AND 10 flights -> 6 percent (counting the 2025-04 trip would reach 15,160.00 and 12, the top tier); baseline 0 gives 78.10. | companion_fare_lounge_credit (parameter, cross-difficulty club): Summit Club Executive -> 12.00; baseline 0 gives 83.67. | companion_fare_rebooking_goodwill (parameter): 1 Crestline-cancellation reinstatement -> 12.00; baseline 0 gives 83.67. | companion_fare_holder_fare_credit (parameter, cross-difficulty ticket): own ticketed card fare 289.00 -> 5.00; baseline 0 gives 76.67. | non-factor: product_fare = 119.00; result = 71.67. || TAXES: taxes_ticket_tax_base_method (method): call-center booking without Hawaii surcharge -> 7.5 percent of 71.67 + 6.29 = 5.85; the baseline (fare alone) gives 15.58. | taxes_cardholder_credit (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty loyalty): card-anniversary certificate AND 46000.00 miles -> 6.00; baseline 0 gives 22.05. | taxes_rebooking_credit (parameter): 2 booking entries -> 3.00; baseline 0 gives 19.05. | taxes_frequent_flyer_credit (parameter, cross-difficulty loyalty): 10 flights in 12 months -> 4.00; baseline 0 gives 20.05. | non-factor: gross_taxes = 29.05; result = 16.05. || Whole-baseline fall-backs: refund 0.00, phone fee 23.79, fare 119.00, taxes 28.58 - all differ from gold. Multi-source: companion_fare_activity_discount (qualifying dollars AND flights) and taxes_cardholder_credit (issue source AND card miles). Cross-difficulty: loyalty, club and ticket (the holder's own ticketed card fare). Near-misses: the 2025-04 Phoenix trip (12 whole months back, outside the window that counts months 0 to 11; counting it reaches 15,160.00 qualifying dollars and 12 flights, the top activity and flyer tiers), the 2025-04-20 co-brand accrual of 18,000 miles (outside; counting it reaches 64,000, the top card tiers), the flown tickets paid by card (not ticketed, so not the holder-fare ticket), and booking 1's charges (most recent until booking 2's are paid).

[4 Base-invariant card] refund_once: c1_phone has no refund naming it at frozen_time (booking 1's two refunds name c1_fare and c1_tax) -> satisfied, correlated through reversed_entry_id. No base gate applies to companion_fare_charge (booking gates govern companion_trip_redeem, which booking 2 already passed on 2026-04-27: active certificate, book-by 2026-09-10, 64 days ahead against 14 minimum, no blackout, membership active). No time gate applies.

[5 Business-object card] Targets: booking 2 (redeem 2026-04-27, companion ticket 4194006093312, travel 2026-06-30, call center) for the three charges; booking 1's phone fee charge c1_phone (14.50, ticket 4194004410528) for the refund. Excluded: booking 1's fare and taxes charges and their 2026-03-05 refunds (settled, naming c1_fare/c1_tax). Each charge names ticket 4194006093312; the refund names c1_phone.

[6 Seed rows] customers; loyalty_holdings Summit Gold enrolled 2016-09-02 (mile_balance 185,280 = seeded accruals, qualifying_dollars_ytd 3,560.00 = 2026 accruals after the reset); 12 flight + 12 qualifying-dollar accruals of 6 flown trips and 5 co-brand accruals; club_holdings Summit Club Executive; ticket_holdings 6 flown tickets plus the holder's ticketed 4194006093311 (base 289.00, residual 331.30) with its one fare collection; companion_holdings (used, trips 0) and 9 ledger entries. Automatic clauses checked: no expiry (book-by 2026-09-10), no revocation, booking 1 settled except its phone fee, which this tree refunds.

[7 Problem-tree card] Root companion_ext_booking_taxes_and_fees (owner=user). Edges, all value_input and state form: (a) taxes <- companion fare, gate fare_posted_for_tax, 'The taxes and fees of a companion booking are fixed only after the certificate's ledger carries that booking's companion fare charge.' (b) taxes <- phone fee, gate phone_posted_for_tax, 'For a booking made through the reservations call center, the taxes and fees are not worked out until the certificate's ledger also carries that booking's phone booking fee charge.' (c) phone fee <- phone fee refund, gate standing_phone_fees, 'The phone booking fee of a new booking is fixed only after the certificate's ledger carries the phone booking fee refund owed on every booking of that certificate that Crestline cancelled.' Each passes the four-point test (ordering connective; a record-visible charge or refund entry; no tool, id or code token; scope exactly the booking or the Crestline-cancelled bookings). Exactly one write brings each state about (a companion fare charge only by the fare policy's tool, a phone fee charge only by the phone policy's, a phone fee refund only by the refund policy's). Directions: two affirmative, one negated. Owners: fare, phone fee and taxes are the holder's payments (owner=user); the refund is the desk's. Deletion sensitivity (actual run): Skipping the fare write (step 14) and replaying the rest unchanged, companion_ext_booking_taxes_and_fees computes 18.16 instead of 16.05.; Skipping the phone write (step 12) and replaying the rest unchanged, companion_ext_booking_taxes_and_fees computes 16.66 instead of 16.05.; Skipping the rphone write (step 10) and replaying the rest unchanged, companion_ext_booking_phone_fee computes 0.00 instead of 6.29.. Parallel branches commute (alternative order gives {'fare': 71.67, 'rphone': 13.29, 'phone': 6.29, 'tax': 16.05}, same terminal hash).

[8 Persona design] Owen Radcliffe, talkative retired coach; volunteers the goal (pay what is outstanding on Elena's companion ticket after the declined card) and the email's wording about taxes and fees. Gives 3035554726 and 80124 to locate and verify; email, date of birth, certificate and Summit numbers, Elena's ticket name, trip and lounge membership only when asked; the March Crestline cancellation only if asked about earlier use. Passive: agrees to settle everything outstanding, thanks the agent for money coming back, pays exactly what is handed over, ends when told the ticket is fully paid. No asks beyond the payment.

[9 Standard solution] Locate, verify, read the certificate, ledger, Summit membership and activity, Summit Club, tickets and the holder ticket's fare history. Refund 13.29 naming c1_phone; hand over the phone fee 6.29; hand over the companion fare 71.67; hand over the taxes and fees 16.05, each against ticket 4194006093312.

[10 Verification runs] Same scripts as task 0 (gate build_env/eval_compute on the replayed handling-time world). Output: refund 13.29 (baselines 0.00/12.22/12.76/12.22, all 0.00); phone fee 6.29 (16.79/4.54/10.79/9.29, all 23.79); fare 71.67 (82.86/78.10/83.67/83.67/76.67, all 119.00); taxes 16.05 (15.58/22.05/19.05/20.05, all 28.58); skip runs 18.16, 16.66, 0.00. Seeded history computed the same way: booking 1 fare 99.86, phone fee 14.50, taxes 21.78 on 2026-01-14; refunds 99.86 and 21.78 on 2026-03-05.

[11 Draft recomputation from the visible context] From the published rules, tool schemas, finder returns and persona alone: the taxes rule points at the unpaid fare and phone fee; the phone fee rule points at the unrefunded phone fee of the Crestline-cancelled booking; each amount reproduces with the windows counted back from 2026-04-28 and 'most recent' entries read after each payment. One reading only.

[Gate runs] Per-task, from the repository root with DIFF=env/env_0020_national_network_airline/tasks/companion_certificates_and_passes: check_extended.py $DIFF --task 1 -> EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools.py $DIFF --task 1 -> TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK (4 tools); replay_tasks.py $DIFF --task 1 -> 17 actions, deterministic, non-vacuous, 0 errors, closure 51 = initial 51, REPLAY OK; check_solvability.py $DIFF --task 1 -> verify True, 4 calls, 11 base gates, 10 seed rows, SOLVABILITY OK; check_compute.py $DIFF --task 1 -> 4 computations, 17 factors, 10 cross-difficulty, 16 history rows, 57 branches, COMPUTE OK; check_grounding.py $DIFF --task 1 -> 2 identity attributes, 4 answers absent from the persona, 7 conditional cues, GROUNDING OK; check_cross_fire.py $DIFF --task 1 -> SCOPE OK. Difficulty-wide run without --task: EXTENDED OK (8 policies, 8 tools, 2 tasks, disjoint scopes covering every policy), TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK (suite means branches 54.00 and steps 16.50, history_rows_max 36, branches_max 57), GROUNDING OK, CACHE-DIFF INFO (no cache trap designed), SCOPE OK. check_traceability.py is run only after the KB is published.

[Rework round 2, audit audits/policy_task/companion_certificates_and_passes] Task 1 PASSED; charter-wide F1 (rounding mode unstated) was fixed for all eight policies: every rule now states rounding half up to the cent and every RND in compute rounds x + 0.0000001. Re-run on this world: refund 13.29, phone fee 6.29, fare 71.67, taxes 16.05 and every factor and skip figure unchanged (no intermediate here is an exact half cent: 10.6333, 13.2875, 100.674, 10.5, 5.847). The seeded history (99.86, 14.50, 21.78, 99.86, 21.78) was re-evaluated on its own dates under the half-up compute and is unchanged. 1.md observation 2: [3] now says the April 2025 trip is 12 whole months back. Observation 1 (the opening ask 'what is outstanding' covers the fare and phone fee as the customer's own need): kept - the persona names neither charge, both taxes edges bear weight and fix the payment order, and the phone fee refund is reachable only through its prerequisite sentence. Observation 3 (P8 pro-rates a refund over the claim window): kept as a published claim-window rule.
user_scenario:
You are Owen Radcliffe, 57, a retired high-school baseball coach from Castle Rock - friendly, a little talkative, and keen to get things squared away. Yesterday afternoon you phoned Crestline and booked your wife Elena as your companion on your New Orleans trip leaving June 30, using the companion certificate that came with your Crestline card. Your own ticket went through, but the card on file was declined for Elena's part, and this morning's email says the taxes and fees on her companion ticket are still waiting for payment and to call Crestline to complete it. You have a new card in hand. You open by saying you want to pay what is outstanding on Elena's companion ticket so it is all set. You do not know any of the amounts and you never guess one.
To look you up you give your phone number, 3035554726; to verify, you give that phone number and your ZIP code, 80124, and if asked for more, your email owen.radcliffe@outlook.com or your date of birth 1968-11-03. Only if asked do you mention that the certificate number is CMP42260915, your Summit number is 4219907735, Elena is on the ticket as RADCLIFFE/ELENA MARIE, the trip is Denver to New Orleans and back leaving June 30 and was booked by phone yesterday, and you have a Summit Club Executive lounge membership. If you are asked whether the certificate was used before, you recall that Crestline cancelled your and Elena's Boston trip the night before you were due to fly in early March and that you did not rebook it then.
If the agent explains that more than the taxes and fees is still unpaid on Elena's ticket, you say you figured the whole thing had bounced and you are glad to settle all of it. If the agent tells you some money is going back to you from the March trip, you say that is decent of them and thank them, without asking for anything more. Each time the agent hands you a payment to make, you complete it yourself with exactly the certificate, ticket number and amount the agent gives you, on your new card, and read back the confirmation if asked. Once the agent tells you Elena's ticket is fully paid, you thank them and end the call. You never bring up the March trip's fees or refunds yourself, you never question how an amount is worked out, and you ask for nothing beyond paying for Elena's ticket.
